## Preventive Dental Care & Checkups in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/preventive-care.html

Regular exams and professional cleanings to keep your teeth healthy and stop gum disease before it starts.


One of the easiest ways to prevent the decline of your oral health is to maintain a regular schedule of having your teeth cleaned by our dental hygienist. A professional cleaning minimizes the accumulation of harmful plaque and calculus on your teeth, and your hygienist will give you instruction on personalized home care.

By working together, we can prevent the advance of gum disease and help ensure healthy teeth and a beautiful smile in the years ahead. We care for patients of all ages — from children to senior adults.

### Why Preventive Dental Care Matters

Tooth decay and gum disease usually start quietly. In the early stages you may not feel any pain at all, which is why routine visits are so valuable: small problems are easier, more comfortable and less costly to treat when they are found early.

Regular cleanings remove hardened plaque (calculus) that brushing and flossing can’t reach. Left in place, it irritates the gums and can lead to [periodontal (gum) disease](https://dentalasheville.com/periodontics.html), which destroys the bone that supports your teeth.

### Preventive & Diagnostic Services We Offer

#### Examinations and Consultations
Dr. Holcombe checks your teeth, gums, bite and existing dental work, then talks with you about what he sees and any treatment options so you can make informed decisions.

#### Professional Dental Cleanings
Your hygienist removes plaque and calculus above and below the gumline and polishes your teeth, then shows you techniques tailored to your mouth.

#### Dental Radiographs (X-rays)
X-rays reveal what can’t be seen during a visual exam, such as decay between teeth, infection at the root and bone levels. We take them only as often as your individual needs call for.

#### Oral Cancer Screenings
A quick, painless check of your lips, tongue, cheeks, throat and the floor of your mouth for any unusual changes that should be watched or evaluated further.

#### Sealants
A thin, tooth-colored protective coating on the chewing surfaces of back teeth that helps keep food and bacteria out of deep grooves. Sealants are most often recommended for children and teens.

#### Fluoride Application
A professional fluoride treatment strengthens enamel and helps protect teeth against decay for both children and adults.

### Caring for Your Smile Between Visits

- Brush twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste.
- Clean between your teeth once a day with floss or another interdental cleaner.
- Limit sugary snacks and drinks, especially sipping or snacking throughout the day.
- Avoid tobacco, which raises the risk of gum disease and oral cancer.
- Call us if you notice bleeding gums, sensitivity, a broken tooth or a sore that doesn’t heal.

### What to Expect at Your Checkup

1. **Health history** — We review your medical history, medications and any concerns you have.
2. **Cleaning** — Your hygienist cleans and polishes your teeth and checks your gums.
3. **X-rays as needed** — We take radiographs when they’re due based on your needs.
4. **Exam & screening** — Dr. Holcombe examines your teeth and gums and performs an oral cancer screening.
5. **Your plan** — We explain what we found, answer your questions and recommend your next visit.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How often should I have my teeth cleaned?**
Many patients do well with a checkup and cleaning every six months. If you have a history of gum disease or other risk factors, Dr. Holcombe may recommend more frequent visits. Your schedule is based on your own needs.

**Are dental X-rays safe?**
Dental X-rays use a very low dose of radiation. We take them only when they will provide information needed for your care, and how often depends on your individual risk for problems.

**Who should get dental sealants?**
Sealants are most commonly placed on the permanent back teeth of children and teens, whose deep grooves are prone to cavities. Some adults benefit too. We’ll let you know if sealants are a good fit.

**What happens during an oral cancer screening?**
Dr. Holcombe looks at and gently feels the tissues of your mouth, tongue and throat for lumps, patches or sores. It takes only a few minutes and is part of your routine exam.

**Do you see children?**
Yes. We would like to take care of your entire family, from children to senior adults.

## Cosmetic Dentistry in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/cosmetic-dentistry.html

Teeth whitening, tooth-colored fillings, veneers, crowns and bridges to help you smile with confidence.


We understand the importance of being able to smile with confidence. A great smile is one of the best ways to make a positive impression, which is why we offer a wide variety of treatments to help give you the smile you want.

Every cosmetic plan starts with a conversation about your goals and an exam to make sure your teeth and gums are healthy enough to support the result you want.

### Cosmetic Treatments We Offer

#### Teeth Whitening
Whitening helps you have a brighter, whiter smile. Teeth naturally change color over time and also become discolored from coffee, tea, red wine and smoking. Whitening is not for every situation, but we would love to discuss whether it could benefit you.

#### Tooth-Colored Fillings
We offer resin composite fillings that blend in with your natural tooth, so repairs from cavities or small chips are hard to notice.

#### Veneers
Veneers cover the front surface of a tooth to change its shape or color. They can improve teeth that are stained, chipped, worn or slightly uneven.

#### Crowns
A crown covers and protects a cracked, damaged or heavily filled tooth, restoring its strength and appearance. Crowns are also commonly recommended after a [root canal](https://dentalasheville.com/root-canals.html) on a back tooth.

#### Bridges
A bridge spans the gap where a tooth is missing, anchored to the teeth on each side. It replaces the missing tooth and makes chewing easier. A bridge can also be supported by [dental implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html) instead of natural teeth.

### Is Cosmetic Dentistry Right for You?

You may benefit from a cosmetic consultation if you have:

- Stained or yellowed teeth
- Chipped, cracked or worn teeth
- Teeth that are uneven or oddly shaped
- A gap from a missing tooth
- Older fillings that are dark or easy to see
If we find decay or gum disease during your exam, we’ll treat that first through [preventive care](https://dentalasheville.com/preventive-care.html) or [gum treatment](https://dentalasheville.com/periodontics.html) so your cosmetic work lasts.

### Caring for Your Results

- Brush twice daily and clean between your teeth every day.
- After whitening, limit coffee, tea, red wine and tobacco to keep your shade longer.
- Avoid chewing ice, pens or other hard objects that can chip teeth and restorations.
- Keep up with regular checkups so we can monitor crowns, bridges, veneers and fillings.

### Your Cosmetic Consultation

1. **Talk about your goals** — Tell us what you’d like to change about your smile.
2. **Exam** — Dr. Holcombe checks the health of your teeth and gums.
3. **Review options** — We explain which treatments fit your goals, along with the pros and cons of each.
4. **Your plan** — Together we choose a plan, and you decide what’s right for you.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Is professional teeth whitening safe?**
Whitening under a dentist’s guidance is a common and generally safe way to brighten natural teeth. Some people have temporary sensitivity. We’ll check that whitening is appropriate for your teeth before you start.

**Will whitening change the color of my crowns or fillings?**
No. Whitening works on natural tooth enamel and does not change the color of crowns, veneers or fillings. If you have visible restorations, we’ll talk through how to keep everything matching.

**What’s the difference between a veneer and a crown?**
A veneer covers only the front surface of a tooth and is mainly used to improve appearance. A crown covers the entire tooth and is used when a tooth needs extra strength and protection as well.

**Can you replace my old silver fillings with tooth-colored ones?**
Often, yes. Dr. Holcombe will check your existing fillings and let you know whether replacing them with tooth-colored composite makes sense.

**How long do crowns and bridges last?**
With good home care and regular checkups, crowns and bridges can last many years. How long depends on your bite, habits and oral hygiene.

## Dental Implants in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html

Implant crowns, bridges, denture attachments and fixed hybrids to replace missing teeth.


With dental implants you can rediscover your confidence to eat, speak, laugh and enjoy life. Implants are titanium screws that attach to the bone where you are missing teeth, allowing a natural-looking, tooth-colored restoration to be secured in the space.

Our office offers a range of implant restorations — from a single crown to a full arch of teeth — and Dr. Holcombe will help you understand which option fits your mouth, goals and budget.

### What Is a Dental Implant?

A dental implant has three parts: a titanium post that sits in the jawbone and acts like a tooth root, a connector, and the restoration you see — a crown, bridge or denture. Once the bone has bonded with the post, the implant provides a strong, stable base for your new teeth.

### Implant Restorations We Offer

#### Implant Crowns and Bridges
These are similar to a traditional crown or bridge, except the restoration sits on the implant instead of your natural tooth.

#### Implant Attachments for Dentures
Implants can be used as attachments for [traditional dentures](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html), allowing them to “snap” into place. This increases the stability and retention of the denture.

#### Fixed Hybrids
A fixed hybrid replaces all or most of the teeth in an arch. Unlike a denture, you don’t take it out — it is screwed into place on the implants. It is more stable and smaller than a traditional denture, making it a great alternative for patients who struggle with a gag reflex.

### Benefits of Dental Implants

- Look, feel and function much like natural teeth
- Replace a tooth without reshaping the neighboring teeth, as a traditional bridge requires
- Help preserve the jawbone, which tends to shrink where teeth are missing
- Let you eat, speak and laugh without worrying about slipping teeth
- Can stabilize a loose denture or replace it with a fixed option

### Are You a Candidate for Implants?

Most adults who are missing one or more teeth can be evaluated for implants. Good candidates generally have healthy gums and enough jawbone to support the implant. Smoking, uncontrolled diabetes and some medications can affect healing, so we’ll review your health history carefully.

If you have active gum disease, we’ll treat it first through [periodontal therapy](https://dentalasheville.com/periodontics.html). If a failing tooth needs to come out, we can start with an [extraction](https://dentalasheville.com/oral-surgery.html).

### Caring for Your Implants

Implants can’t get cavities, but the gums and bone around them can become inflamed just like natural teeth. Brush twice a day, clean around the implant daily and keep up with [regular cleanings and checkups](https://dentalasheville.com/preventive-care.html) so we can monitor the implant and your restoration.

### The Dental Implant Process

1. **Consultation** — Dr. Holcombe examines your mouth, reviews X-rays and discusses your options and timeline.
2. **Implant placement** — The implant is placed in the jawbone. We’ll explain every step of placement during your consultation.
3. **Healing** — Over the following months, the bone bonds with the implant to create a solid foundation.
4. **Your new teeth** — Your custom crown, bridge, denture attachment or fixed hybrid is attached to the implant.
5. **Ongoing care** — Routine checkups and cleanings help your implant last.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long do dental implants last?**
With good home care and regular checkups, implants can last for many years. The crown or other restoration on top may eventually need to be replaced due to normal wear.

**Does getting an implant hurt?**
The area is numbed for the procedure, and many patients find the discomfort afterward manageable. We’ll explain what to expect and how to stay comfortable during healing.

**Should I choose an implant or a bridge?**
Both replace missing teeth. An implant stands on its own and doesn’t require reshaping neighboring teeth, while a traditional bridge is anchored to the teeth on either side. Dr. Holcombe will help you weigh the pros and cons for your situation.

**Can implants help my loose denture?**
Yes. A few implants can serve as attachments that let your denture snap securely into place, or support a fixed hybrid that stays in. Learn more about our [denture options](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html).

**Do I need one implant for every missing tooth?**
Not necessarily. Implant bridges and fixed hybrids can replace several teeth using fewer implants.

## Complete & Partial Dentures in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html

Complete and partial dentures, including implant-supported options, so you can chew and smile again.


If you have lost several teeth and can’t chew and smile like you once did, we have options to help. We can replace all your teeth with a complete denture or make a partial denture that works with your existing teeth.

We can also incorporate [dental implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html) into the denture design to help it stay in place, providing a more secure fit.

### Denture Options

#### Complete Dentures
A full set of replacement teeth for the upper jaw, lower jaw or both, for patients who are missing all of their teeth in an arch.

#### Partial Dentures
A removable appliance that fills the gaps left by missing teeth and attaches to your remaining natural teeth. It also helps keep those teeth from shifting.

#### Implant-Retained (Snap-In) Dentures
Implants act as anchors so your denture “snaps” into place, improving stability and chewing. [Learn about dental implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html).

#### Fixed Hybrids
For patients who want teeth that don’t come out, a fixed hybrid screws onto implants and replaces all or most of the teeth in an arch.

### Signs Dentures May Help

- You are missing several teeth or all teeth in an arch
- Chewing is difficult or painful
- Remaining teeth are badly decayed, loose or failing
- Your current denture is loose, uncomfortable or worn

### Adjusting to & Caring for Your Dentures

- Start with soft foods cut into small pieces, then work back to your usual diet.
- Practice speaking and reading aloud — your tongue and cheeks adapt quickly.
- Call us if you develop a sore spot; a simple adjustment usually helps.
- Clean your denture daily with a denture brush and keep it moist when it’s out of your mouth.
- Follow Dr. Holcombe’s instructions about removing your denture at night to let your gums rest.
- Keep regular checkups. Your mouth changes over time, and dentures may need relining or replacing.

### Getting Your Dentures

1. **Exam & planning** — We evaluate your teeth, gums and bone and talk through your options.
2. **Preparing your mouth** — If needed, we remove failing teeth and smooth the bone with [alveoloplasty](https://dentalasheville.com/oral-surgery.html) so your denture fits better.
3. **Impressions & bite** — We record the shape of your mouth and how your jaws come together.
4. **Try-in** — You preview the fit, look and bite before the denture is finished.
5. **Delivery & adjustments** — We fit your new denture and make adjustments as you get used to it.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does it take to get used to new dentures?**
Most people need a few weeks to feel comfortable eating and speaking with new dentures. Sore spots are common at first and can usually be fixed with a quick adjustment.

**What is the difference between complete and partial dentures?**
A complete denture replaces all the teeth in an arch. A partial denture replaces some missing teeth and attaches to your remaining natural teeth.

**Should I sleep in my dentures?**
Many patients are advised to remove dentures at night to let the gums rest and to keep the denture clean. Dr. Holcombe will give you instructions for your specific denture.

**Will my dentures need to be replaced?**
Over time the gums and bone under a denture change shape, so dentures may need to be relined or remade to keep a good fit. Regular checkups help us catch this early.

**How can implants make my denture more secure?**
Implants placed in the jaw can act as attachments that hold your denture firmly in place. See our [dental implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html) page for details.

---

## Tooth Extractions & Oral Surgery in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/oral-surgery.html

Tooth extractions, surgical root tip extractions and alveoloplasty, performed in our office.


Oral surgery is needed in many situations, such as removing wisdom teeth, preparing the mouth for dentures, or extracting infected and non-restorable teeth.

We offer extractions and alveoloplasty — shaping of the bone after an extraction to help a denture fit better — in a comfortable, friendly setting.

### Oral Surgery Procedures We Offer

#### Tooth Extractions
Removal of a tooth that is badly damaged, infected or can’t be saved.

#### Surgical Root Tip Extractions
Removal of a broken root or root tip that remains in the bone after a tooth has fractured.

#### Alveoloplasty
Smoothing and reshaping the jawbone after extractions so that [dentures](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html) fit comfortably and securely.

### When Is a Tooth Extraction Needed?

- Severe decay or a fracture that can’t be repaired
- Infection that can’t be treated another way
- Advanced gum disease that has loosened the tooth
- Wisdom teeth that are causing problems
- Preparing the mouth for dentures
Whenever possible, we try to save your natural tooth — for example with a [root canal](https://dentalasheville.com/root-canals.html) and crown. If an extraction is the best choice, we’ll talk about replacing the tooth with an [implant](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html), a [bridge](https://dentalasheville.com/cosmetic-dentistry.html) or a [denture](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html).

Dr. Holcombe will evaluate your wisdom teeth and let you know whether they can be removed in our office or whether a referral to an oral surgeon is the better choice.

### Recovering After an Extraction

- Bite gently on gauze to help a blood clot form.
- Rest for the remainder of the day and keep your head elevated.
- For the first few days, avoid straws, smoking and forceful spitting, which can dislodge the clot and cause a painful “dry socket.”
- Use an ice pack on the outside of your cheek to reduce swelling.
- Eat soft foods and chew on the other side.
- Take any medications exactly as directed.
- Call us if you have heavy bleeding, increasing pain or swelling, or a fever.

### What to Expect

1. **Exam & X-rays** — We evaluate the tooth and surrounding bone and explain your options.
2. **Numbing** — Local anesthetic numbs the area so you feel pressure, not pain.
3. **Removal** — The tooth or root tip is gently removed, and the bone is smoothed if needed.
4. **Aftercare** — You go home with gauze and clear written instructions.
5. **Replacement plan** — We discuss options to replace the tooth if needed.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Does a tooth extraction hurt?**
The area is fully numbed, so you should feel pressure but not sharp pain during the procedure. Some soreness afterward is normal and usually improves over a few days.

**How long does it take to recover from an extraction?**
Most people feel much better within a few days after a simple extraction. Surgical extractions can take a little longer. Following your aftercare instructions helps you heal well.

**What is a dry socket?**
A dry socket happens when the blood clot in the extraction site is dislodged too early, exposing the bone. It can be quite painful. Avoiding straws, smoking and forceful spitting for the first few days lowers the risk. Call us if you think you have one.

**Should I replace a tooth that was extracted?**
Usually, yes. A gap can let neighboring teeth shift and make chewing harder. Options include [implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html), [bridges](https://dentalasheville.com/cosmetic-dentistry.html) and [partial dentures](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html).

**What is alveoloplasty?**
Alveoloplasty is the smoothing and reshaping of the jawbone, typically after extractions, so a denture fits better and more comfortably.

## Gum Disease Treatment (Periodontics) in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/periodontics.html

Scaling and root planing, periodontal surgery and other treatments for gum disease.


Slow but progressive, periodontal disease swells the gums (gingiva) and destroys the bone that supports your teeth. Once the bone is lost, it does not regenerate. The disease may be generalized, affecting all of your teeth, or localized to a single tooth.

Gum disease affects men and women of all ethnicities, from the teen years through adulthood. In its early stages you may be unaware of it — which is why regular exams matter.

### Signs of Gum Disease

- Gums that bleed when you brush or floss
- Red, swollen or tender gums
- Persistent bad breath
- Gums pulling away from the teeth
- Loose or shifting teeth

### What Raises Your Risk?

Dental hygiene habits, medications, smoking, alcohol, diet, general health and heredity can all play a role in how gum disease progresses. Conditions such as diabetes are also associated with gum disease.

### Periodontal Treatments We Offer

#### Scaling & Root Planing
A deep cleaning that removes plaque and calculus from below the gumline and smooths the root surfaces so the gums can heal and reattach.

#### Periodontal Surgery
When deep cleaning isn’t enough, surgical treatment can help reach and clean deeper areas and reduce pockets around the teeth.

#### Gingival Medicament Placement
Medication placed directly into gum pockets to help control bacteria and support healing.

#### Gingivoplasty
Reshaping of the gum tissue to restore healthier contours that are easier to keep clean.

### Keeping Your Gums Healthy After Treatment

Gum disease can be controlled, but it needs ongoing care. Many patients need periodontal maintenance cleanings more often than twice a year. At home, brush twice daily, clean between your teeth every day and avoid tobacco.

Healthy gums are also important if you’re considering [dental implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html), since the tissue around implants can become inflamed too.

### What to Expect

1. **Gum measurements** — We gently measure the pockets around each tooth to check for gum disease.
2. **X-rays** — Radiographs show the level of bone supporting your teeth.
3. **Treatment plan** — Dr. Holcombe explains the findings and recommends treatment.
4. **Treatment** — Deep cleaning or other therapy is completed, with the area numbed for comfort.
5. **Maintenance** — Regular follow-up cleanings help keep the disease under control.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Can gum disease be reversed?**
Gingivitis, the earliest stage, can often be reversed with professional cleanings and good home care through [preventive care](https://dentalasheville.com/preventive-care.html). Periodontitis can be treated and controlled, but bone that has been lost does not grow back — so early treatment matters.

**Is scaling and root planing painful?**
The area is numbed so you stay comfortable during treatment. Your gums may be tender for a few days afterward.

**How often will I need cleanings after treatment?**
Many patients with a history of gum disease need maintenance cleanings more often than twice a year. Dr. Holcombe will recommend a schedule based on how your gums respond.

**Is gum disease linked to other health problems?**
Research has found associations between gum disease and conditions such as diabetes and heart disease. Keeping your gums healthy is part of caring for your overall health.

**Can gum disease cause tooth loss?**
Yes. As gum disease destroys the supporting bone, teeth can loosen, shift and eventually be lost. If teeth are lost, options include [implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html) and [dentures](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html).

---

## Root Canal Treatment in Asheville, NC

URL: https://dentalasheville.com/root-canals.html

Remove damaged nerve tissue, relieve pain and save your natural tooth.


A root canal is needed when decay or trauma has irreversibly damaged the nerve inside a tooth. The nerve cannot heal itself, so the tooth either needs a root canal or must be extracted.

If it isn’t treated promptly, an extremely painful and dangerous infection called a dental abscess may develop. Root canal treatment removes the infection and lets you keep your natural tooth.

### Signs You May Need a Root Canal

- A persistent or throbbing toothache
- Sensitivity to hot or cold that lingers
- Pain when biting or chewing
- Swollen or tender gums near a tooth
- A tooth that has darkened in color
- A small bump or pimple on the gum
Sometimes there are no symptoms at all, and the problem is found on an X-ray during a routine checkup.

### Saving Your Natural Tooth

Keeping your own tooth is usually the best option when it can be saved. If a tooth can’t be saved, we’ll discuss an [extraction](https://dentalasheville.com/oral-surgery.html) and replacement options such as a [dental implant](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html).

### After Your Root Canal

- Some tenderness for a few days is normal.
- Avoid chewing hard foods on the tooth until it has its final restoration.
- Take any medications as directed.
- Call us if you notice swelling or worsening pain.
- Keep brushing, flossing and visiting us for regular checkups.

### The Root Canal Procedure

1. **Exam & X-rays** — We confirm the diagnosis and explain your options.
2. **Numbing** — Local anesthetic keeps you comfortable.
3. **Cleaning the canal** — The damaged and infected nerve tissue is removed and the canal is disinfected.
4. **Sealing** — The canal is filled with a sterile material to seal it from bacteria.
5. **Protecting the tooth** — For back teeth, we normally recommend a [crown](https://dentalasheville.com/cosmetic-dentistry.html) to strengthen and protect the tooth.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Is a root canal painful?**
Root canal treatment is done with local anesthetic, and its purpose is to relieve the pain caused by an infected or damaged nerve. Most patients feel some tenderness for a few days afterward.

**Is it better to have a root canal or pull the tooth?**
When a tooth can be saved, keeping it is usually best for chewing and for preventing neighboring teeth from shifting. If extraction is the better choice, we’ll discuss [implants](https://dentalasheville.com/dental-implants.html), [bridges](https://dentalasheville.com/cosmetic-dentistry.html) and [partial dentures](https://dentalasheville.com/dentures.html) to replace it.

**Will I need a crown after a root canal?**
For back teeth, we normally recommend a crown, because a tooth that has had a root canal can become brittle and is more likely to crack.

**What happens if I wait?**
The infection won’t heal on its own. Waiting can lead to a dental abscess, more pain and a greater chance of losing the tooth.

**How long will a tooth with a root canal last?**
With a proper final restoration, good home care and regular checkups, a tooth that has had a root canal can last for many years.
